subject: Proposal: converting Acme Cloud from monthly to annual commit — pricing & ramp playbook
messages:
From: Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.com>
To: Alicia Moreno <alicia@acmecloud.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 25 Jun 2025 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Converting to an annual commit — draft plan and numbers

Hi Alicia — great to meet last week. Per our call, I pulled together a short playbook for switching Acme Cloud from monthly billing to an annual committed plan and a suggested ramp schedule your finance team can review. Attached is the one-pager (Redwood-Annual-Commit-Playbook.pdf) and a draft SOW with sample invoice cadence.

High-level proposal:
- Term: 12 months (option to extend to 24 months for deeper discount)
- Commit: estimated 3M tokens/month baseline (we can define a sliding ramp)
- Pricing idea: 18% discount vs current month-to-month list for year 1 at the committed volume; 10% list discount thereafter if you extend to year 2.
- Ramp schedule option A (conservative): 60% of committed usage in Q1, 85% by Q3; option B (aggressive): 80% by Q1, 100% by Q2.

Key asks for procurement to confirm: preferred invoice cadence (annual upfront vs quarterly billing on committed amount), PO process and whether they require a tax-exempt certificate, and any required CLIN terms (billing code) for SOW.

If procurement prefers monthly invoicing on a committed annual contract, we can support monthly invoices but will adjust discount by -3 percentage points. If they pay annual upfront, we can increase the year-1 discount to 22% and include a single free migration credit worth $15k applied to first invoice.

Next step: can you introduce a procurement contact or share the procurement email and three preferred invoice models (monthly-on-commit, quarterly-on-commit, annual-upfront)? I can then work with Ben on the pricing redline and route to Marcus for executive approval.

Thanks — Neha

--
Neha Kapoor
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
neha@redwood.com | (415) 555-0192
From: Alicia Moreno <alicia@acmecloud.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 01 Jul 2025 11:07:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Converting to an annual commit — draft plan and numbers

Neha — thanks for the materials; I shared with our procurement and finance leads. A couple quick clarifications from our side before I loop them in:

1) Procurement asked whether the discount bands you quoted are additive with volume tiers or if they replace them — i.e., if we overperform commit by 20%, do we get the higher tier pricing for overage?
2) They prefer annual upfront from a vendor-management perspective but need to run that through the treasury team (cashflow constraints). If we cannot do annual upfront, they will ask for quarterly billing on the committed amount. Would your -3pp adjustment to discount apply to quarterly as well?
3) For multi-year asks: procurement mentioned 24 months with a 30% discount target; they asked if Redwood can provide a firm cap on price increases year-over-year.

Procurement contact: procurement@acmecloud.com (I copied them on this thread). We also need a short playbook paragraph that we can paste into our SOW describing the ramp protections and how overage is invoiced. Could you add that to the SOW?

Appreciate the fast turnaround — Alicia

--
Alicia Moreno
Head of Product Partnerships, Acme Cloud
alicia@acmecloud.com
From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
To: procurement@acmecloud.com, Alicia Moreno <alicia@acmecloud.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 04 Jul 2025 09:53:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Converting to an annual commit — draft plan and numbers

Hi Alicia / procurement team — thanks for the questions. A few clarifications and our counter-proposal so procurement has something concrete to review: 

Answers:
- Discount & overage: discounts apply to committed units only. Overage is billed at an overage rate which is the committed unit price + 30% (standard). If you prefer blended pricing on actual volume, we can provide a blended rate for any given invoice period (we typically reserve blended for >20% sustained overage).
- Quarterly billing: the -3 percentage points off the quoted discount applies to any non-upfront billing cadence (monthly or quarterly).
- Multi-year cap: we can commit to a price increase cap of +5% year-over-year on list unit price for any renewal term, provided the customer maintains or increases committed volume. For 24-month deals we propose a two-tier discount: 20% year 1 (annual upfront), 15% year 2. If you need 30% total, we can get there only through higher upfront payment or a 36-month term.

Our suggested counter (for procurement to consider):
- Term: 12 months, annual upfront preferred (sample invoice attached).
- Commit: 36M tokens/year (3M/month baseline) with a quarter-based ramp: Q1 = 50% of monthly baseline, Q2 = 75%, Q3 = 100% (gives room for validation).
- Discount: 20% year-1 (annual upfront); if treasury cannot do annual upfront, quarterly billing reduces discount to 17%.
- Migration credit: $15k if annual upfront.
- Overage handling: monthly invoiced overage at committed unit price + 30% with blended option if sustained >20% for 3 consecutive months.

Ben — can you review legal redlines? Marcus — if this is acceptable I think we can present to procurement and get a PO in 2–3 weeks.

Thanks,
Ben

--
Ben Carter
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
ben@redwood.com
From: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 15 Jul 2025 15:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Converting to an annual commit — draft plan and numbers

Thanks team — reviewed. A couple operational notes and an approval boundary: 

1) Approve the counter as written (20% year-1 annual upfront / 17% if quarterly) for deals <= $400k ARR equivalent. Anything above that requires VP sign-off. This saves time for mid-market conversions.
2) Approve the 5% YoY cap for 2-year renewals provided the customer keeps or ups their commit. For 24-month asks that demand 30% off, we should propose a 36-month program or an upfront funding credit model; do not concede to 30% on 24 months as-is.
3) Finance: instruct billing to prepare both an annual upfront invoice and a quarterly-committed invoice template. Neha — when procurement confirms the cadence, send me the final SOW and I will sign the sales approval matrix.

Ben / Neha, please include the following paragraph in the SOW under "Ramp & Overage Protections":

"Ramp & Overage Protections: Customer will declare a committed monthly token baseline at contract signature. Initial ramp will follow the agreed quarterly percentages. Overage during any invoice period will be invoiced at the committed unit price plus 30%. If customer sustains >20% overage for three consecutive months, Redwood will engage to propose a blended rate or adjust the committed baseline to reflect actual usage. Any refunds or credits will be limited to billing errors and will not be issued for expected production variance."
Send the final SOW and I'll route for execution.

Marcus Lin
VP, Revenue — Redwood Inference
marcus@redwood.com
